paper_id: Ma et al. - 2012 - Sherlock is around Detecting network failures with local evidence fusion
title: Sherlock is Around: Detecting Network Failures with Local Evidence Fusion
motivation: Sink-based diagnosis incurs huge transmission overhead; self-diagnosis has narrow scope and inconsistent results from different nodes
problem_framing: Balance diagnosis workload among sensor nodes while achieving integrated judgment through distributed evidence fusion in local areas
key_insight: Root causes can be partly reflected within a neighborhood; D-S theory with similarity-based weighting achieves associative fusion regardless of order
method_signature: Local-Diagnosis (LD2): Naive Bayesian Classifier + improved Dempster-Shafer evidence fusion via fusion tree
evaluation_criteria: False negative rate (miss detection) and false positive rate (false alarm) on 50-node TelosB testbed
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Existing self-diagnosis leads to inconsistent results; TinyD2 fails to achieve consensus as density increases
evidence_for_taste: sink often fails to obtain complete evidences
TinyD2 often fails to achieve a consensus
thinking_moves: 把诊断范围从全局sink收窄到局部邻域,利用邻居节点覆盖同一根因的不同侧面
引入D-S理论处理多节点判断冲突,并改进其结合规则支持结合律以容忍融合树结构动态变化
用相似度加权替代修改组合规则,避免引入额外参数调优
cites_own_work: Liu et al. 2011 - Self-diagnosis for large scale wireless sensor networks
